Luk.8.47.bsb: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
Luk.8.47.kjv: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.

Luk.8.48.bsb: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
Luk.8.48.kjv: And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

Luk.9.38.bsb: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.
Luk.9.38.kjv: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.

Luk.9.39.bsb: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.
Luk.9.39.kjv: And, lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him.

Luk.9.40.bsb: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
Luk.9.40.kjv: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.

Luk.9.41.bsb: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
Luk.9.41.kjv: And Jesus answering said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.

Luk.9.42.bsb: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
Luk.9.42.kjv: And as he was yet a coming, the devil threw him down, and tare him. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.

Luk.18.15.bsb: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
Luk.18.15.kjv: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

Luk.18.16.bsb: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Luk.18.16.kjv: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

Luk.7.31.bsb: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
Luk.7.31.kjv: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

Luk.7.32.bsb: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
Luk.7.32.kjv: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.

Luk.18.20.bsb: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”
Luk.18.20.kjv: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.

Luk.9.48.bsb: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”
Luk.9.48.kjv: And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

Luk.9.46.bsb: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.
Luk.9.46.kjv: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.

Luk.9.47.bsb: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.
Luk.9.47.kjv: And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,

Luk.18.10.bsb: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
Luk.18.10.kjv: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

Luk.24.53.bsb: praising God continually in the temple.
Luk.24.53.kjv: And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

Luk.13.6.bsb: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.
Luk.13.6.kjv: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

Luk.13.7.bsb: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
Luk.13.7.kjv: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

Luk.13.8.bsb: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
Luk.13.8.kjv: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

Luk.13.9.bsb: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’”
Luk.13.9.kjv: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

Luk.6.5.bsb: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Luk.6.5.kjv: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

Luk.20.17.bsb: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
Luk.20.17.kjv: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?

Luk.20.18.bsb: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
Luk.20.18.kjv: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

Luk.22.3.bsb: Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
Luk.22.3.kjv: Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.

Luk.22.4.bsb: And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.
Luk.22.4.kjv: And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.

Luk.22.5.bsb: They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
Luk.22.5.kjv: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

Luk.22.6.bsb: Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd.
Luk.22.6.kjv: And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.

Luk.22.24.bsb: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them should be considered the greatest.
Luk.22.24.kjv: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.

Luk.22.25.bsb: So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.
Luk.22.25.kjv: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

Luk.22.26.bsb: But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
Luk.22.26.kjv: But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

Luk.22.27.bsb: For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.
Luk.22.27.kjv: For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.

Luk.22.28.bsb: You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.
Luk.22.28.kjv: Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.

Luk.22.29.bsb: And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me,
Luk.22.29.kjv: And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;

Luk.22.30.bsb: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Luk.22.30.kjv: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Luk.7.22.bsb: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
Luk.7.22.kjv: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

Luk.1.73.bsb: the oath He swore to our father Abraham, to grant us
Luk.1.73.kjv: The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,

Luk.20.34.bsb: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
Luk.20.34.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:

Luk.20.37.bsb: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
Luk.20.37.kjv: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

Luk.20.38.bsb: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
Luk.20.38.kjv: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.

Luk.23.39.bsb: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”
Luk.23.39.kjv: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

Luk.23.40.bsb: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
Luk.23.40.kjv: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

Luk.23.41.bsb: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
Luk.23.41.kjv: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

Luk.12.36.bsb: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
Luk.12.36.kjv: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.

Luk.12.37.bsb: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
Luk.12.37.kjv: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.

Luk.23.27.bsb: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
Luk.23.27.kjv: And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.

Luk.23.28.bsb: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
Luk.23.28.kjv: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

Luk.23.29.bsb: Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!’
Luk.23.29.kjv: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

Luk.23.30.bsb: At that time ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!” and to the hills, “Cover us!”’
Luk.23.30.kjv: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

Luk.23.31.bsb: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
Luk.23.31.kjv: For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Luk.23.32.bsb: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
Luk.23.32.kjv: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.

Luk.23.35.bsb: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
Luk.23.35.kjv: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

Luk.23.36.bsb: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
Luk.23.36.kjv: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,

Luk.23.37.bsb: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
Luk.23.37.kjv: And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.

Luk.23.38.bsb: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Luk.23.38.kjv: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

Luk.23.44.bsb: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
Luk.23.44.kjv: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.

Luk.23.45.bsb: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
Luk.23.45.kjv: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.

Luk.23.47.bsb: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man.”
Luk.23.47.kjv: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

Luk.23.48.bsb: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.
Luk.23.48.kjv: And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.

Luk.23.49.bsb: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.
Luk.23.49.kjv: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things.

Luk.16.23.bsb: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
Luk.16.23.kjv: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

Luk.16.24.bsb: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
Luk.16.24.kjv: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

Luk.16.25.bsb: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
Luk.16.25.kjv: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

Luk.16.26.bsb: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
Luk.16.26.kjv: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

Luk.16.27.bsb: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,
Luk.16.27.kjv: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

Luk.16.28.bsb: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
Luk.16.28.kjv: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

Luk.16.18.bsb: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Luk.16.18.kjv: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.

Luk.17.10.bsb: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”
Luk.17.10.kjv: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.

Luk.21.3.bsb: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
Luk.21.3.kjv: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:

Luk.21.4.bsb: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
Luk.21.4.kjv: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.

Luk.10.25.bsb: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Luk.10.25.kjv: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

Luk.10.26.bsb: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”
Luk.10.26.kjv: He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?

Luk.10.27.bsb: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
Luk.10.27.kjv: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.

Luk.10.28.bsb: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”
Luk.10.28.kjv: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

Luk.10.29.bsb: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Luk.10.29.kjv: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?

Luk.10.30.bsb: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
Luk.10.30.kjv: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

Luk.10.31.bsb: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
Luk.10.31.kjv: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

Luk.10.32.bsb: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
Luk.10.32.kjv: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.

Luk.10.36.bsb: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
Luk.10.36.kjv: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?

Luk.10.37.bsb: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
Luk.10.37.kjv: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

Luk.7.50.bsb: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
Luk.7.50.kjv: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

Luk.17.5.bsb: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
Luk.17.5.kjv: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.

Luk.18.8.bsb: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”
Luk.18.8.kjv: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?

Luk.12.22.bsb: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
Luk.12.22.kjv: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.

Luk.12.23.bsb: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
Luk.12.23.kjv: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.

Luk.12.24.bsb: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
Luk.12.24.kjv: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?

Luk.12.25.bsb: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
Luk.12.25.kjv: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

Luk.12.26.bsb: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Luk.12.26.kjv: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?

Luk.12.27.bsb: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
Luk.12.27.kjv: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

Luk.12.28.bsb: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
Luk.12.28.kjv: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

Luk.12.29.bsb: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
Luk.12.29.kjv: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

Luk.12.30.bsb: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
Luk.12.30.kjv: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

Luk.12.31.bsb: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
Luk.12.31.kjv: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.

Luk.12.32.bsb: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
Luk.12.32.kjv: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

Luk.17.6.bsb: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
Luk.17.6.kjv: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.

Luk.2.25.bsb: Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
Luk.2.25.kjv: And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him.

Luk.2.26.bsb: The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
Luk.2.26.kjv: And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

Luk.2.33.bsb: The Child’s father and mother were amazed at what was spoken about Him.
Luk.2.33.kjv: And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.

Luk.2.35.bsb: so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your soul as well.”
Luk.2.35.kjv: (Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.

Luk.6.46.bsb: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
Luk.6.46.kjv: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

Luk.6.47.bsb: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
Luk.6.47.kjv: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

Luk.6.48.bsb: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.
Luk.6.48.kjv: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

Luk.6.49.bsb: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
Luk.6.49.kjv: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

Luk.7.9.bsb: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
Luk.7.9.kjv: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

Luk.5.5.bsb: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
Luk.5.5.kjv: And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.

Luk.7.4.bsb: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,
Luk.7.4.kjv: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

Luk.7.6.bsb: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
Luk.7.6.kjv: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:

Luk.7.7.bsb: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
Luk.7.7.kjv: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

Luk.7.8.bsb: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
Luk.7.8.kjv: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

Luk.5.4.bsb: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
Luk.5.4.kjv: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

Luk.18.35.bsb: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
Luk.18.35.kjv: And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:

Luk.18.36.bsb: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
Luk.18.36.kjv: And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant.

Luk.18.37.bsb: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.
Luk.18.37.kjv: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.

Luk.18.39.bsb: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Luk.18.39.kjv: And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

Luk.18.40.bsb: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had come near, Jesus asked him,
Luk.18.40.kjv: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,

Luk.17.11.bsb: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
Luk.17.11.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.

Luk.17.15.bsb: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
Luk.17.15.kjv: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,

Luk.17.16.bsb: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
Luk.17.16.kjv: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.

Luk.17.17.bsb: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
Luk.17.17.kjv: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

Luk.17.18.bsb: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
Luk.17.18.kjv: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.

Luk.17.19.bsb: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
Luk.17.19.kjv: And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.

Luk.5.18.bsb: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
Luk.5.18.kjv: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

Luk.5.19.bsb: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
Luk.5.19.kjv: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

Luk.5.20.bsb: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
Luk.5.20.kjv: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

Luk.7.36.bsb: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
Luk.7.36.kjv: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.

Luk.7.37.bsb: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
Luk.7.37.kjv: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,

Luk.7.39.bsb: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”
Luk.7.39.kjv: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.

Luk.7.40.bsb: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.
Luk.7.40.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Master, say on.

Luk.7.41.bsb: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
Luk.7.41.kjv: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

Luk.7.42.bsb: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”
Luk.7.42.kjv: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?

Luk.7.43.bsb: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.
Luk.7.43.kjv: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.

Luk.7.44.bsb: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
Luk.7.44.kjv: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.

Luk.7.45.bsb: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
Luk.7.45.kjv: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

Luk.7.46.bsb: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
Luk.7.46.kjv: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.

Luk.7.47.bsb: Therefore I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”
Luk.7.47.kjv: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

Luk.7.48.bsb: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Luk.7.48.kjv: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.

Luk.7.49.bsb: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
Luk.7.49.kjv: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?

Luk.10.38.bsb: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
Luk.10.38.kjv: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

Luk.10.39.bsb: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.
Luk.10.39.kjv: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

Luk.10.40.bsb: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”
Luk.10.40.kjv: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

Luk.10.41.bsb: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.
Luk.10.41.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

Luk.10.42.bsb: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
Luk.10.42.kjv: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

Luk.9.20.bsb: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
Luk.9.20.kjv: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.

Luk.9.21.bsb: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
Luk.9.21.kjv: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;

Luk.9.37.bsb: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.
Luk.9.37.kjv: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.

Luk.8.22.bsb: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.
Luk.8.22.kjv: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples: and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.

Luk.8.23.bsb: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
Luk.8.23.kjv: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water, and were in jeopardy.

Luk.8.24.bsb: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.
Luk.8.24.kjv: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.

Luk.8.25.bsb: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”
Luk.8.25.kjv: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.

Luk.8.26.bsb: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
Luk.8.26.kjv: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.

Luk.1.54.bsb: He has helped His servant Israel, remembering to be merciful,
Luk.1.54.kjv: He hath holpen his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy;

Luk.1.55.bsb: as He promised to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants forever.”
Luk.1.55.kjv: As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.

Luk.1.68.bsb: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and redeemed His people.
Luk.1.68.kjv: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,

Luk.1.69.bsb: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David,
Luk.1.69.kjv: And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;

Luk.1.72.bsb: to show mercy to our fathers and to remember His holy covenant,
Luk.1.72.kjv: To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;

Luk.2.49.bsb: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?”
Luk.2.49.kjv: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?

Luk.10.21.bsb: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
Luk.10.21.kjv: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.

Luk.10.22.bsb: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
Luk.10.22.kjv: All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

Luk.11.13.bsb: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
Luk.11.13.kjv: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

Luk.24.49.bsb: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”
Luk.24.49.kjv: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.

Luk.1.53.bsb: He has filled the hungry with good things, but has sent the rich away empty.
Luk.1.53.kjv: He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away.

Luk.18.19.bsb: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
Luk.18.19.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God.

Luk.1.66.bsb: And all who heard this wondered in their hearts and asked, “What then will this child become?” For the Lord’s hand was with him.
Luk.1.66.kjv: And all they that heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him.

Luk.1.49.bsb: For the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is His name.
Luk.1.49.kjv: For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.

Luk.16.15.bsb: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
Luk.16.15.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

Luk.13.34.bsb: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
Luk.13.34.kjv: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

Luk.20.9.bsb: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
Luk.20.9.kjv: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.

Luk.20.10.bsb: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
Luk.20.10.kjv: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.

Luk.20.11.bsb: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
Luk.20.11.kjv: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.

Luk.20.12.bsb: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
Luk.20.12.kjv: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.

Luk.20.13.bsb: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’
Luk.20.13.kjv: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.

Luk.20.14.bsb: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
Luk.20.14.kjv: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.

Luk.20.15.bsb: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
Luk.20.15.kjv: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?

Luk.20.16.bsb: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
Luk.20.16.kjv: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.

Luk.15.4.bsb: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
Luk.15.4.kjv: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

Luk.15.5.bsb: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,
Luk.15.5.kjv: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

Luk.15.6.bsb: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’
Luk.15.6.kjv: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

Luk.15.11.bsb: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.
Luk.15.11.kjv: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

Luk.15.12.bsb: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
Luk.15.12.kjv: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.

Luk.15.13.bsb: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
Luk.15.13.kjv: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

Luk.15.14.bsb: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
Luk.15.14.kjv: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.

Luk.15.15.bsb: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
Luk.15.15.kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

Luk.15.16.bsb: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
Luk.15.16.kjv: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

Luk.15.17.bsb: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but here I am, starving to death!
Luk.15.17.kjv: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

Luk.15.18.bsb: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
Luk.15.18.kjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

Luk.15.19.bsb: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’
Luk.15.19.kjv: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

Luk.15.20.bsb: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
Luk.15.20.kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

Luk.15.21.bsb: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
Luk.15.21.kjv: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

Luk.15.22.bsb: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Luk.15.22.kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

Luk.15.23.bsb: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
Luk.15.23.kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

Luk.15.24.bsb: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
Luk.15.24.kjv: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

Luk.15.25.bsb: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
Luk.15.25.kjv: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.

Luk.15.26.bsb: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
Luk.15.26.kjv: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

Luk.15.27.bsb: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
Luk.15.27.kjv: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

Luk.1.50.bsb: His mercy extends to those who fear Him, from generation to generation.
Luk.1.50.kjv: And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation.

Luk.1.77.bsb: to give to His people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,
Luk.1.77.kjv: To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins,

Luk.6.36.bsb: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Luk.6.36.kjv: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

Luk.1.51.bsb: He has performed mighty deeds with His arm; He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
Luk.1.51.kjv: He hath shewed strength with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.

Luk.11.20.bsb: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Luk.11.20.kjv: But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

Luk.18.27.bsb: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
Luk.18.27.kjv: And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.

Luk.12.6.bsb: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
Luk.12.6.kjv: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?

Luk.12.7.bsb: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Luk.12.7.kjv: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

Luk.22.35.bsb: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” “Nothing,” they answered.
Luk.22.35.kjv: And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing.

Luk.22.52.bsb: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?
Luk.22.52.kjv: Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?

Luk.22.53.bsb: Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.”
Luk.22.53.kjv: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.

Luk.22.54.bsb: Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
Luk.22.54.kjv: Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.

Luk.22.55.bsb: When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.
Luk.22.55.kjv: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.

Luk.22.56.bsb: A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. “This man also was with Him,” she said.
Luk.22.56.kjv: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.

Luk.22.57.bsb: But Peter denied it. “Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.
Luk.22.57.kjv: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.

Luk.22.58.bsb: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
Luk.22.58.kjv: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.

Luk.22.59.bsb: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”
Luk.22.59.kjv: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.

Luk.22.60.bsb: “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replied. And immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
Luk.22.60.kjv: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.

Luk.22.61.bsb: And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word that the Lord had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”
Luk.22.61.kjv: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

Luk.22.63.bsb: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
Luk.22.63.kjv: And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him.

Luk.22.65.bsb: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him.
Luk.22.65.kjv: And many other things blasphemously spake they against him.

Luk.22.66.bsb: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,
Luk.22.66.kjv: And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together, and led him into their council, saying,

Luk.22.67.bsb: “If You are the Christ, tell us.” Jesus answered, “If I tell you, you will not believe.
Luk.22.67.kjv: Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe:

Luk.22.68.bsb: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
Luk.22.68.kjv: And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go.

Luk.22.69.bsb: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
Luk.22.69.kjv: Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.

Luk.3.1.bsb: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
Luk.3.1.kjv: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Cesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Iturea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,

Luk.20.25.bsb: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
Luk.20.25.kjv: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which be Cesar’s, and unto God the things which be God’s.

Luk.3.22.bsb: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
Luk.3.22.kjv: And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

Luk.12.12.bsb: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”
Luk.12.12.kjv: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.

Luk.1.41.bsb: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Luk.1.41.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost:

Luk.9.25.bsb: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?
Luk.9.25.kjv: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?

Luk.19.47.bsb: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.
Luk.19.47.kjv: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,

Luk.20.1.bsb: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
Luk.20.1.kjv: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,

Luk.20.2.bsb: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”
Luk.20.2.kjv: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?

Luk.20.3.bsb: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:
Luk.20.3.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:

Luk.20.4.bsb: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”
Luk.20.4.kjv: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?

Luk.20.5.bsb: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
Luk.20.5.kjv: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?

Luk.20.6.bsb: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
Luk.20.6.kjv: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.

Luk.20.7.bsb: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
Luk.20.7.kjv: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.

Luk.20.8.bsb: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
Luk.20.8.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

Luk.24.27.bsb: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
Luk.24.27.kjv: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

Luk.3.15.bsb: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.
Luk.3.15.kjv: And as the people were in expectation, and all men mused in their hearts of John, whether he were the Christ, or not;

Luk.13.35.bsb: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
Luk.13.35.kjv: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

Luk.19.43.bsb: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
Luk.19.43.kjv: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,

Luk.21.5.bsb: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,
Luk.21.5.kjv: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,

Luk.21.6.bsb: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
Luk.21.6.kjv: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

Luk.21.7.bsb: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
Luk.21.7.kjv: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?

Luk.21.8.bsb: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.
Luk.21.8.kjv: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

Luk.21.9.bsb: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.”
Luk.21.9.kjv: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

Luk.21.10.bsb: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
Luk.21.10.kjv: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

Luk.21.11.bsb: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
Luk.21.11.kjv: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

Luk.21.12.bsb: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.
Luk.21.12.kjv: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.

Luk.21.13.bsb: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.
Luk.21.13.kjv: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.

Luk.21.14.bsb: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.
Luk.21.14.kjv: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:

Luk.21.15.bsb: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
Luk.21.15.kjv: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

Luk.21.16.bsb: You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.
Luk.21.16.kjv: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.

Luk.21.17.bsb: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.
Luk.21.17.kjv: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.

Luk.21.19.bsb: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.
Luk.21.19.kjv: In your patience possess ye your souls.

Luk.21.20.bsb: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.
Luk.21.20.kjv: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

Luk.21.21.bsb: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.
Luk.21.21.kjv: Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

Luk.21.22.bsb: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
Luk.21.22.kjv: For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

Luk.21.23.bsb: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
Luk.21.23.kjv: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.

Luk.21.24.bsb: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
Luk.21.24.kjv: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

Luk.21.25.bsb: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.
Luk.21.25.kjv: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

Luk.15.28.bsb: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
Luk.15.28.kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.

Luk.15.29.bsb: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
Luk.15.29.kjv: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

Luk.15.30.bsb: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
Luk.15.30.kjv: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.

Luk.15.31.bsb: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
Luk.15.31.kjv: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

Luk.15.32.bsb: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
Luk.15.32.kjv: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

Luk.3.17.bsb: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
Luk.3.17.kjv: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.

Luk.10.10.bsb: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
Luk.10.10.kjv: But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,

Luk.10.11.bsb: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
Luk.10.11.kjv: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

Luk.10.12.bsb: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
Luk.10.12.kjv: But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

Luk.10.13.bsb: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
Luk.10.13.kjv: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

Luk.10.14.bsb: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
Luk.10.14.kjv: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.

Luk.11.31.bsb: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
Luk.11.31.kjv: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

Luk.11.32.bsb: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
Luk.11.32.kjv: The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

Luk.12.2.bsb: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
Luk.12.2.kjv: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

Luk.12.3.bsb: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
Luk.12.3.kjv: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

Luk.12.4.bsb: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
Luk.12.4.kjv: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

Luk.12.5.bsb: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
Luk.12.5.kjv: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.

Luk.13.24.bsb: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
Luk.13.24.kjv: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

Luk.13.25.bsb: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
Luk.13.25.kjv: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

Luk.13.26.bsb: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
Luk.13.26.kjv: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

Luk.13.27.bsb: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
Luk.13.27.kjv: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

Luk.13.28.bsb: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
Luk.13.28.kjv: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

Luk.13.29.bsb: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
Luk.13.29.kjv: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

Luk.19.12.bsb: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.
Luk.19.12.kjv: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

Luk.19.13.bsb: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.
Luk.19.13.kjv: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

Luk.19.14.bsb: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’
Luk.19.14.kjv: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

Luk.19.15.bsb: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
Luk.19.15.kjv: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.

Luk.19.16.bsb: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’
Luk.19.16.kjv: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

Luk.19.17.bsb: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
Luk.19.17.kjv: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

Luk.19.18.bsb: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
Luk.19.18.kjv: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.

Luk.19.19.bsb: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’
Luk.19.19.kjv: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.

Luk.19.20.bsb: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.
Luk.19.20.kjv: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:

Luk.19.21.bsb: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
Luk.19.21.kjv: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.

Luk.19.22.bsb: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
Luk.19.22.kjv: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:

Luk.19.23.bsb: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’
Luk.19.23.kjv: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?

Luk.19.24.bsb: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
Luk.19.24.kjv: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.

Luk.19.25.kjv: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)

Luk.19.26.bsb: He replied, ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
Luk.19.26.kjv: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.

Luk.20.45.bsb: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
Luk.20.45.kjv: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,

Luk.20.46.bsb: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
Luk.20.46.kjv: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;

Luk.20.47.bsb: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
Luk.20.47.kjv: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.

Luk.9.5.bsb: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
Luk.9.5.kjv: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.

Luk.10.15.bsb: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
Luk.10.15.kjv: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

Luk.11.49.bsb: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
Luk.11.49.kjv: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:

Luk.11.51.bsb: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
Luk.11.51.kjv: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

Luk.12.47.bsb: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
Luk.12.47.kjv: And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.
