Luk.13.5.bsb: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”
Luk.13.5.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

Luk.15.1.bsb: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.
Luk.15.1.kjv: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

Luk.15.2.bsb: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
Luk.15.2.kjv: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

Luk.15.3.bsb: Then Jesus told them this parable:
Luk.15.3.kjv: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

Luk.15.8.bsb: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
Luk.15.8.kjv: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?

Luk.15.9.bsb: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’
Luk.15.9.kjv: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

Luk.24.47.bsb: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.
Luk.24.47.kjv: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

Luk.6.45.bsb: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
Luk.6.45.kjv: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

Luk.18.17.bsb: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
Luk.18.17.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.

Luk.6.22.bsb: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Luk.6.22.kjv: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.

Luk.6.23.bsb: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
Luk.6.23.kjv: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

Luk.18.29.bsb: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
Luk.18.29.kjv: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God’s sake,

Luk.18.30.bsb: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”
Luk.18.30.kjv: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.

Luk.19.45.bsb: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.
Luk.19.45.kjv: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;

Luk.14.27.bsb: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
Luk.14.27.kjv: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

Luk.14.28.bsb: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
Luk.14.28.kjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

Luk.14.29.bsb: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,
Luk.14.29.kjv: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,

Luk.14.30.bsb: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
Luk.14.30.kjv: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

Luk.14.31.bsb: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
Luk.14.31.kjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

Luk.14.32.bsb: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
Luk.14.32.kjv: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

Luk.14.33.bsb: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.
Luk.14.33.kjv: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

Luk.16.16.bsb: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
Luk.16.16.kjv: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.

Luk.12.38.bsb: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
Luk.12.38.kjv: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

Luk.12.39.bsb: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
Luk.12.39.kjv: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.

Luk.12.40.bsb: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
Luk.12.40.kjv: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

Luk.12.41.bsb: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”
Luk.12.41.kjv: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?

Luk.12.42.bsb: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
Luk.12.42.kjv: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?

Luk.12.43.bsb: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
Luk.12.43.kjv: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

Luk.12.44.bsb: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
Luk.12.44.kjv: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.

Luk.12.45.bsb: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
Luk.12.45.kjv: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

Luk.12.46.bsb: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
Luk.12.46.kjv: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.

Luk.17.7.bsb: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
Luk.17.7.kjv: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?

Luk.17.8.bsb: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink’?
Luk.17.8.kjv: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

Luk.17.9.bsb: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
Luk.17.9.kjv: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.

Luk.16.1.bsb: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
Luk.16.1.kjv: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

Luk.16.2.bsb: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
Luk.16.2.kjv: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

Luk.16.3.bsb: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
Luk.16.3.kjv: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.

Luk.16.4.bsb: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
Luk.16.4.kjv: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

Luk.16.5.bsb: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
Luk.16.5.kjv: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

Luk.16.6.bsb: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager, ‘sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
Luk.16.6.kjv: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.

Luk.16.7.bsb: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
Luk.16.7.kjv: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.

Luk.16.8.bsb: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
Luk.16.8.kjv: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.

Luk.16.10.bsb: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
Luk.16.10.kjv: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

Luk.16.11.bsb: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
Luk.16.11.kjv: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

Luk.16.12.bsb: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
Luk.16.12.kjv: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

Luk.16.13.bsb: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
Luk.16.13.kjv: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

Luk.10.7.bsb: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
Luk.10.7.kjv: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

Luk.8.17.bsb: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
Luk.8.17.kjv: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.

Luk.8.14.bsb: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
Luk.8.14.kjv: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

Luk.5.24.bsb: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins…” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
Luk.5.24.kjv: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.

Luk.6.8.bsb: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
Luk.6.8.kjv: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

Luk.11.17.bsb: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
Luk.11.17.kjv: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.

Luk.12.51.bsb: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
Luk.12.51.kjv: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

Luk.12.52.bsb: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
Luk.12.52.kjv: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

Luk.12.53.bsb: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
Luk.12.53.kjv: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

Luk.12.58.bsb: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
Luk.12.58.kjv: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.

Luk.12.59.bsb: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.”
Luk.12.59.kjv: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

Luk.12.11.bsb: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
Luk.12.11.kjv: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:

Luk.4.15.bsb: He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone.
Luk.4.15.kjv: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.

Luk.4.23.bsb: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”
Luk.4.23.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.

Luk.4.29.bsb: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.
Luk.4.29.kjv: And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.

Luk.4.30.bsb: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way.
Luk.4.30.kjv: But he passing through the midst of them went his way,

Luk.4.31.bsb: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.
Luk.4.31.kjv: And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.

Luk.4.33.bsb: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
Luk.4.33.kjv: And in the synagogue there was a man, which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and cried out with a loud voice,

Luk.13.10.bsb: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
Luk.13.10.kjv: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

Luk.13.11.bsb: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
Luk.13.11.kjv: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.

Luk.13.12.bsb: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
Luk.13.12.kjv: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

Luk.13.13.bsb: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
Luk.13.13.kjv: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

Luk.13.14.bsb: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
Luk.13.14.kjv: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

Luk.1.5.bsb: In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
Luk.1.5.kjv: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.

Luk.1.6.bsb: Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.
Luk.1.6.kjv: And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.

Luk.1.7.bsb: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.
Luk.1.7.kjv: And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.

Luk.1.21.bsb: Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he took so long in the temple.
Luk.1.21.kjv: And the people waited for Zacharias, and marvelled that he tarried so long in the temple.

Luk.1.22.bsb: When he came out and was unable to speak to them, they realized he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them but remained unable to speak.
Luk.1.22.kjv: And when he came out, he could not speak unto them: and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: for he beckoned unto them, and remained speechless.

Luk.1.57.bsb: When the time came for Elizabeth to have her child, she gave birth to a son.
Luk.1.57.kjv: Now Elisabeth’s full time came that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.

Luk.1.58.bsb: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
Luk.1.58.kjv: And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.

Luk.1.59.bsb: On the eighth day, when they came to circumcise the child, they were going to name him after his father Zechariah.
Luk.1.59.kjv: And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.

Luk.1.60.bsb: But his mother replied, “No! He shall be called John.”
Luk.1.60.kjv: And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.

Luk.1.61.bsb: They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who bears this name.”
Luk.1.61.kjv: And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.

Luk.1.62.bsb: So they made signs to his father to find out what he wanted to name the child.
Luk.1.62.kjv: And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.

Luk.1.63.bsb: Zechariah asked for a tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they were all amazed.
Luk.1.63.kjv: And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.

Luk.1.64.bsb: Immediately Zechariah’s mouth was opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak, praising God.
Luk.1.64.kjv: And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.

Luk.2.23.bsb: (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”),
Luk.2.23.kjv: (As it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;)

Luk.2.24.bsb: and to offer the sacrifice specified in the Law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
Luk.2.24.kjv: And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.

Luk.2.39.bsb: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
Luk.2.39.kjv: And when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

Luk.4.9.bsb: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.
Luk.4.9.kjv: And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:

Luk.4.12.bsb: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Luk.4.12.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

Luk.19.46.bsb: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
Luk.19.46.kjv: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.

Luk.5.25.bsb: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
Luk.5.25.kjv: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.

Luk.8.39.bsb: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
Luk.8.39.kjv: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee. And he went his way, and published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him.

Luk.7.11.bsb: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
Luk.7.11.kjv: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

Luk.7.12.bsb: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
Luk.7.12.kjv: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

Luk.23.55.bsb: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
Luk.23.55.kjv: And the women also, which came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulchre, and how his body was laid.

Luk.23.56.bsb: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
Luk.23.56.kjv: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.

Luk.24.1.bsb: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
Luk.24.1.kjv: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.

Luk.24.2.bsb: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
Luk.24.2.kjv: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.

Luk.24.3.bsb: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
Luk.24.3.kjv: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

Luk.24.4.bsb: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.
Luk.24.4.kjv: And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments:

Luk.24.5.bsb: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
Luk.24.5.kjv: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?

Luk.24.7.bsb: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”
Luk.24.7.kjv: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

Luk.9.9.kjv: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
